title: Prove generic dirty-connector rigidity under paid invertible frames
body:
## Result and exact scope

Add one operation family to the generic dirty-connector contract: paid invertible connector-only frames `z <- Rz`. A phase-normalization proof shows that arbitrary interleaved frames cannot achieve the five-source/all-31-mask **72-map-call paired endpoint**. The exact unit-token optimum stays **74**, or **76** if at least one nonidentity frame must be used.

The operation word and frame matrices are fixed independently of the arbitrary A/B map entries. This is not a lower bound for operator-specialized charts or a physical runtime optimum. The 76 upper bound deliberately uses a redundant inverse frame pair; it is not advertised as a useful improvement.

The package includes the full noncommutative coefficient argument, complete weighted cost screen, smallest two-bit dirty shear pilot and meaningful controls. Pilot invoices are **14 versus 12 scalar XORs**, or **194 versus 168** in the explicit complete fixed-port tariff. A deliberately retained order-three control shows why arbitrary framed words do **not** inherit even map-call parity.

## Assignment, source pins and overlap

- Task: `connector-alphabet-change`, scoped package `research/connector-frame-rigidity`.
- Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected record and all frozen sources unchanged.
- `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json` and `VERIFY.json` record the scope, exact source blobs/SHA256 hashes and registered replay.
- Credit Ross Richardson's universal connector / PR943–PR934 lineage for the original interface, paired-prefix criterion and sharp five-source exclusion. Its 945-pairing census is an inherited regression control, not this contribution's novelty.
- Closest overlap: woklerx's #1858, checked open at `4b650a8471c38f87519da497019dde24228c7f8a`. That construction assumes related fixed maps `B1=R B0`; this generic operator-independent obstruction neither refutes it nor claims priority for adding connector frames.
- Cached publication search covered 558 open PRs and 529 discussion records; freshness and non-exhaustive-code-coverage limitations are documented. No novelty guarantee is inferred from search.
- Coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1884

## Actual verification

On CPython 3.12.12 / Darwin arm64, after the final critical review and added direct-vector coefficient check:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python scripts/research_package.py --package research/connector-frame-rigidity
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -O -B research/connector-frame-rigidity/verify.py
```

Registered replay: **0.30s**; isolated optimized direct smoke: **0.21s** (single local timings, not benchmarks).

```text
PASS_CONNECTOR_FRAME_RIGIDITY pairings=945 phase_pairs=36 coefficients=9216 two_phase_triples=40 odd_restore=256 dirty_cases=16384 controls=5 unit_optimum=74 used_frame_optimum=76 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/connector-frame-rigidity outcome=negative-result
```

The direct smoke emitted the same scoped receipt. All 16,384 dirty map/input pilot cases include literal scalar lowering and inverse replay. Checks do not rely on Python `assert`. No full repository suite or selected-frontier replay was run.

## Limits and open next questions

The arbitrary-dimension statement is a written proof supported by finite checks, not proof-assistant verification or a multiplication theorem. Whether **73 map calls with at least three frames** can work remains open, particularly for favorable nonuniform prices. Structured charts still require an actual selected-supplier boundary and fully charged native implementation. No supplier admission, selected-frontier change, physical speedup or new kappa is claimed.

Prepared for Adam Gall with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation, experiments and writing. Apache-2.0 under repository contribution terms.
